messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: HIGH - gpu-node-47 kubelet OOM thrash detected. Auto-page to #eng-oncall. Alert details: node=gpu-node-47, reason=KubeletOOM, kernel_logs hint: oom_kill invoked.

pagerduty: PagerDuty incident 788234: eng-oncall -> triggered (ack window 2m)

mike.j: acked. I'm oncall. pulling serial and kubelet logs now. pinging infra.

mike.j: quick snapshot: kubelet is in CrashLoopBackOff, kubelet.service shows repeated OOM kill for kubelet process (cgroup mem limit?). system logs show kworker memory spikes.

mike.j: paste: ```sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 | tail -n 80
Jun 12 12:04:08 gpu-node-47 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2345 (kubelet) score 987 or sacrifice child
Jun 12 12:04:08 gpu-node-47 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
Jun 12 12:04:09 gpu-node-47 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Failed with result 'signal'.```

devon: noted. Could be memory leak in kubelet or bad eviction thresholds. Any pids for model-serving containers?

mike.j: running `kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-node-47` - we have 6 model-serving pods (models: embedder-v3, gen-2) and a few infra daemons.

mike.j: attempting cordon+drain to move traffic off, but drain failing on pods with local storage.```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-47
kubectl drain gpu-node-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
# error: unable to drain: eviction blocked for pod model-serving-embedder-0: Pod has local PersistentVolumeClaims```

sara.l: thanks. if drain fails, we can isolate node in smart-router. I'll push a temporary routing policy to stop new requests to that host pool.

sara.l: applying routing change: `smart-router set-weight --pool gpu-rack-12 --node gpu-node-47 --weight 0` -> will take effect in ~30s. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: smart-router: weight change applied, node gpu-node-47 weight set to 0. Existing connections will continue until closed.

mike.j: that reduces new traffic. still need to evacuate running pods. trying to evict stateful pods gracefully: `kubectl delete pod model-serving-embedder-0 --grace-period=60` -> stuck on local-pv unlink. Could force delete but risk data loss.

devon: we can cordon and then restart kubelet to stop thrashing before force deletes. Mike, do you want to try a kubelet restart?

mike.j: restarting kubelet now to reduce memory churn (will cause short transient restarts for kube-proxy). `sudo systemctl restart kubelet` -> kubelet comes back but OOM repeats after ~40s, kernel still invoking oom_kill.

mike.j: kernel dmesg suggests large mem pressure from nvidia driver + blob cache. I've dropped caches and disabled a large local cache process (model shard cache) that was running on that node.

mike.j: `pkill -f shard-cache && echo 3 | sudo tee /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches` - memory freed, kubelet stabilized for now. pods still not evicting due to PVC.

sara.l: good stopgap. I'll open a maintenance ticket and mark node OutOfService in the inventory so autoscaling won't send replacements to same hardware.

sara.l: @support-team I'm going to notify affected customers and recommend failover to their fallback model-pools.

mike.j: customer impact estimate: using logs and router metrics -> 3 customers affected, roughly 12 failed/aborted requests in last 5m, 2 models showing elevated 95p latency (~2.3s -> 6.7s). No full outages yet.

devon: does Dedicated/Private customers see any difference? Router logs show only hosted pool traffic hit this host. We should list which tenants touched: tenant-a, tenant-c, tenant-d (IDs redacted).

mike.j: I'm going to attempt a graceful eviction by scaling down the deployment replicas for model-serving on that node to shift pods to other nodes: `kubectl scale deploy embedder-v3 --replicas=3 --namespace ml` and similar for gen-2.

mike.j: scale ops succeeded, 4 pods rescheduled to other nodes in ~45s. Gen-2 still has one replica stuck due to local PV.

sara.l: if PVC blocks, let's create a replacement PV and bind after copying, but that takes time. For immediate mitigation, we can mark the stuck pod as decomissioned and spin up a new replica on another node, then force-delete the stuck pod (risk accepted). I approve force-delete.

mike.j: force deleting stuck pod now: `kubectl delete pod model-serving-gen2-1 --grace-period=0 --force` -> pod removed. New replica scheduled on gpu-node-51. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty: Incident 788234 acknowledged by mike.j at 12:07 UTC. Escalation suppressed.

devon: thanks. hardware note: I see elevated ECC errors on GPU #2 in the BMC logs during the OOM window. Might be GPU driver leaking pinned memory. Opening a hardware RMA ticket with datacenter ops.

sara.l: oncall handoff plan: mike.j taking initial mitigation and customer triage, sara.l will take over for RMA coordination and post-incident follow-up. devon will continue infra analysis.

mike.j: quick summary for postmortem: root cause suspected: runaway local cache process + driver pinned memory -> node memory pressure -> kubelet OOM -> cascading pod stickiness due to local PVs blocking drain. Mitigation: smart-router weight=0, restart kubelet, kill shard-cache, scale down replicas, force-delete stuck pods, RMA requested.

sara.l: I've notified support and created SEV-22-788234 in ops-tracker with customer list and timeline. Notifying affected customers now with status update: short service degradation, failover in progress, ETA for full remediation 2 hours.

mike.j: logs/commands and timeline I'm pasting to the ticket. Will attach `journalctl -k` and `kubectl describe pod` outputs.

ops-bot: maintenance created: node gpu-node-47 -> state=DECOMMISSIONING, remediation_step=hw-rma, assigned_to=sara.l

sara.l: ok taking over. mike, if anything else pops, ping me directly. devon, can you pull nv driver core dumps for RMA?

devon: will collect and upload to rma ticket. grabbing `sudo nv-dump --collect --out /tmp/gpu47-core.tar.gz` now.

mike.j: leaving notes and handoff in thread. dropping from live. :thumbsup:

sara.l: thanks — I'll keep this thread updated. Once RMA confirmed and node rebuilt we'll uncordon and re-enable routing. Postmortem to follow. :hammer_and_wrench:
